chunks: Erect palaces (thinking) that you will live for ever,

key_terms.تَخْلُدُونَ: You will live eternally or remain forever; from the root kh-l-d, denoting perpetual existence.
key_terms.مَصَانِعَ: Fortresses, palaces, or strongholds; plural of maṣnaʿ, implying places of residence or defense built for permanence.

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'masāniʿ' in Surah Al-Shu'ara?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'masāniʿ' (fortresses or palaces) is often interpreted not merely as physical structures but as symbols of the disbelievers' reliance on material power and worldly stability to defy divine authority. This verse critiques the arrogance of those who believe their accumulated wealth and architectural grandeur can secure them eternal life, contrasting this false permanence with the transient nature of the dunya. It serves as a reminder that true immortality is found in spiritual devotion rather than in the fortification of worldly existence.
